summary: Wednesday's session closed as a market that is still constructive but visibly losing thrust. The composite risk score finished at 41.85, easing 0.25 on the day and keeping the market in a caution state inside a goldilocks regime. At the index level the S&P 500 was flat, giving back record highs set earlier in the session and stalling a 4-day advance, yet beneath the surface dispersion was violent: Nvidia rose 4.70% while AMD fell 6.36% after earnings. The macro and credit backdrop actually improved, with the 10Y yield easing to 4.70 and high-yield spreads tightening to 2.73, but the VIX still ticked up to 16.50 and cross-asset confirmation stayed weak at 0.3333. Model confidence is 0.77 and most feeds are flagged degraded, so read the level as directionally sound rather than precise.

top_risk_drivers.claim: Cross-asset confirmation is the single largest risk contributor at 0.3333: equities, credit and crypto are not moving in a unified direction, so today's index calm rests on a narrow base.
The 10Y real rate at 2.43 sits at the 99.05 percentile of its history, making macro the highest-scoring risk dimension at 76.4 even after today's easing.
The nominal 10Y yield at 4.70 remains a top-three contributor; it slipped 5bp on the day but still prices at the 98.25 percentile of its range.
The VIX rose to 16.50 from 15.86 even though the index finished flat, a sign that hedging demand picked up while headline prices stood still.
Leadership is narrow: the new-highs ratio is only 0.125, so just a small slice of the tracked universe is actually making new highs alongside the index.

supporting_signals.claim: Credit shows no stress at all: high-yield OAS tightened to 2.73 and investment-grade OAS held at 0.78, leaving the liquidity and credit dimension the lowest-risk block at 14.1.
Market structure is intact: 87.5% of tracked names sit above their MA200 and the new-lows ratio is 0.00, so there is no sign of internal deterioration.
The trend block still reads constructive: the index is 9.97% above its MA200, the 52-week drawdown is 0.00, and 3M momentum is 6.66.
The curve stayed positively sloped at 0.45 with the funds rate steady at 3.63, so the day's rate move was a parallel easing rather than a growth scare.

contradicting_signals.claim: Single-name dispersion contradicts the calm index print: Nvidia gained 4.70% to 221.90 while AMD lost 6.36% to 485.61 in the same session, so a flat tape masks a violent rotation.
Breadth quality is worse than the headline suggests: small caps lag by 0.2816 while semis lead by 4.8292, meaning the advance depends on one concentrated theme.
Crypto offered only a token confirmation, with Bitcoin at 64847.00 and Ether at 1917.50 posting gains too small to validate a broad risk-on impulse.

what_changed_today: The composite risk score eased 0.25 to 41.85, holding the caution band for another session.
The S&P 500 gave back record highs set earlier in the day and finished flat, stalling a 4-day advance.
Nvidia jumped 4.70% to 221.90 after SpaceX said it would build its AI exclusively on Nvidia chips, and it carried the Dow.
AMD sank 6.36% to 485.61 after earnings, dragging the Nasdaq even as the Dow set records.
Yields fell across the curve: the 10Y to 4.70, the 2Y to 4.25 and the 10Y real rate to 2.43.
The VIX rose from 15.86 to 16.50 despite the flat close, the day's clearest risk-side divergence.
High-yield spreads tightened from 2.78 to 2.73, extending the benign credit backdrop.
Memory and semis stayed bid, with Micron up 2.40% to 914.09 and Broadcom up 0.93% to 422.05.
watch_next: Whether Nvidia holds its 4.70% endorsement-driven gain; a give-back removes the Dow's main support.
Whether AMD's 6.36% post-earnings drop spreads to the wider semis complex, which still leads by 4.8292.
Whether the VIX extends above 16.50; a sustained move would directly challenge the goldilocks read.
Whether the 10Y stays below 4.75 after slipping to 4.70, since renewed pressure on the 2.43 real rate is the main macro risk.
Whether the new-highs ratio recovers from 0.125 or breadth starts to follow small caps lower.
Data freshness: most feeds are degraded, so confirm the next refresh before acting on the 41.85 reading.

bull_case.title: Bull case: rate relief broadens the rally beyond a handful of AI names
points: Yields eased across the curve, with the 10Y at 4.70, the 2Y at 4.25 and the 10Y real rate at 2.43, which directly relieves macro, the highest-scoring risk dimension at 76.4.
Credit refuses to corroborate any stress: high-yield OAS at 2.73 and investment-grade OAS at 0.78 keep risk premia near cycle lows.
Structure can support a broadening: 87.5% of names are above their MA200, the new-lows ratio is 0.00, and the index is 9.97% above its own MA200.

base_case.title: Base case: caution holds near 41.85 with narrow, rotation-driven leadership
points: The composite stays in the caution band as benign credit and healthy breadth offset an elevated 2.43 real rate.
Index volatility stays contained around a 16.50 VIX while single-name dispersion does the real work, as with Nvidia up 4.70% against AMD down 6.36%.
Cross-asset confirmation stays weak near 0.3333, capping how far the goldilocks regime can extend.

bear_case.title: Bear case: narrow leadership breaks and the macro block reasserts itself
points: If the 2.43 real rate and the 4.70 nominal 10Y resume rising, macro at 76.4 would push the composite out of the caution band.
Leadership is thin enough to cascade: a 0.125 new-highs ratio and small caps lagging by 0.2816 mean a single-name reversal such as AMD's 6.36% drop can spread quickly.
A VIX push above 16.50 alongside 0.3333 cross-asset confirmation would mark the goldilocks regime rolling over.
